title: Brazilian Exports to US Grow 12.1% in August, Driven by Higher Prices
seoTitle: Brazil Exports to US Rise 12.1% in August
subtitle: Total value reached US$3.19 billion in the month new US tariffs took effect
excerpt: Brazilian exports to the United States surged 12.1% in August, reaching a total of US$3.19 billion, primarily bolstered by higher average prices.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In the month that new tariffs from the Donald Trump administration took effect, higher average prices helped sustain the growth of Brazilian sales to the United States. Exports totaled US$3.19 billion for the month, a 12.1% increase.

The 12.1% increase indicates that, despite the change in the tariff regime, Brazilian products maintained competitiveness in the North American market. This performance reflects exporters' ability to adjust to price variations and buyer demand in the United States.

With a total value of US$3.19 billion, bilateral trade demonstrates resilience in the face of newly implemented tariff policies. The scenario highlights the importance of monitoring price evolution and market conditions in the coming periods to understand how Brazilian exports may behave amidst new trade measures.

With information from Agência Brasil.
